## Installation **Command** ```install npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/pagination ``` **Manual** Use React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 with the shadcn semantic colour tokens. Follow the [manual setup guide](https://cadence.dev/docs/installation#manual-installation) for the base CSS and aliases; copying files does not require the shadcn CLI. 1. Install the component's complete recursive npm dependencies (versions are preserved). Example-only packages are listed separately below when needed. ```package-manager npm install clsx tailwind-merge motion @base-ui/react class-variance-authority lucide-react ``` 2. Copy the following registry dependencies in the listed dependency order. Each JSON link exposes every file's full `content` and `target`; copy all files, including multi-file helpers. - [@cadence/cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) — transitive registry dependency. - [@cadence/cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) — direct registry dependency. - [@cadence/cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) — transitive registry dependency. - [@cadence/button](https://cadence.dev/r/button.json) — direct registry dependency. 3. Place every file at its target below. `@components` means your components directory, for example `src/components`; keep the remaining `cadence/` tree and relative imports intact. Each source block on the website copies the entire file, including folded lines. | Item | Target file | Full source | | --- | --- | --- | | cadence-motion | `@components/cadence/lib/motion.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) | | cadence-motion | `@components/cadence/lib/geometry.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) | | cadence-utils | `@components/cadence/lib/cn.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) | | cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/provider.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) | | cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/popup-style.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) | | cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/control-animation.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) | | cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/native-div.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) | | cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/press-button.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) | | button | `@components/cadence/button/index.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/button.json) | | pagination | `@components/cadence/pagination/index.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/pagination.json) | [Source files: cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) [Source files: cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) [Source files: cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) [Source files: button](https://cadence.dev/r/button.json) [Source files: pagination](https://cadence.dev/r/pagination.json) 4. Apply the required CSS/configuration below, then follow [Usage](#usage) for the component imports and composition. No additional item-specific CSS configuration is required beyond the base theme. The provider files above are required imports. Wrapping your application is optional; standalone components respect the system motion preference. To control a subtree, wrap it once: ```tsx import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider"; export function MotionRoot({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) { return {children}; } ``` Copy all ten files in the target list, keeping `pagination/index.tsx` and `button/index.tsx` beside the shared `lib/` directory. Pagination imports `buttonVariants` from the Button module for its anchor styles, so retain that module's complete motion/provider dependency tree even though no `Button` is rendered. The provider files are required imports; wrapping your application is optional. Pagination itself stays static in full, reduced and none modes, with only colour, border and shadow state feedback from the button styles. No additional item-specific CSS is needed beyond the base theme and Tailwind utilities. Keep the source's existing `"use client"` directives. In Next.js App Router, Usage, the collapsed range, custom labels, sizes and boundary examples can be composed in a Server Component with serializable props. “Without a page in the URL” needs its own client module for `useState`, `useId` and the click handler. The top preview has a client boundary already; copying its specimen does not require the site's preview shell. All examples use the same installation files and packages, including `lucide-react` for the component's chevrons and ellipsis; none needs a framework router package. Every page control is a native anchor. The caller supplies destinations, the visible range, `isActive`, boundary states and result data; Pagination does not read the URL, fetch records or calculate pages. Replace the sample query URLs with destinations your application actually handles. The local-state example preserves modified clicks, but its fragment fallback only reaches the results region and cannot restore the selected page when shared or reloaded. At a boundary, omit `href` and keep `role="link"` plus `aria-disabled="true"`; `aria-disabled` alone does not stop an anchor with a destination. Ellipses remain decorative. Give repeated navigation landmarks distinct labels, keep meaningful previous/next accessible names when changing their text, and choose a compact range that fits the parent on narrow screens. ## Usage ```tsx import { Pagination, PaginationContent, PaginationItem, PaginationLink, PaginationNext, PaginationPrevious, } from "@/components/cadence/pagination"; export function ResultPages() { return ( 1 2 3 ); } ``` ## A collapsed range The caller chooses the visible pages and supplies every destination. `PaginationEllipsis` is a decorative skipped range, not a link or a range-expansion control. Here page 2 is current and the last page stays reachable. The sample URLs retain `page` on this documentation route; your application must read that query, fetch the results and derive `isActive` from its actual page. ```tsx import { Pagination, PaginationContent, PaginationEllipsis, PaginationItem, PaginationLink, PaginationNext, PaginationPrevious, } from "@/components/cadence/pagination"; export function CollapsedPages() { return ( 1 2 3 12 ); } ``` ## Custom labels `PaginationPrevious` and `PaginationNext` accept `text`. Back and Forward are visible from `sm` up; below it only the chevrons are visible. When changing the visible text, supply an `aria-label` that includes that text: “Back to previous page” and “Forward to next page” keep the direction clear at either width. The compact composition has its own real anchor destinations. ```tsx import { Pagination, PaginationContent, PaginationItem, PaginationLink, PaginationNext, PaginationPrevious, } from "@/components/cadence/pagination"; export function CustomLabels() { return ( 2 ); } ``` ## Without a page in the URL This caller owns the current page and invoice records; Pagination does not fetch or slice data. An ordinary click or Enter updates the results and `aria-current` without changing the URL. Modified clicks retain the native anchor behavior, whose fragment points to the uniquely named results region; that fallback only scrolls to the region, it cannot restore a local page. Use page query URLs when opening, sharing or reloading must restore the selected results. ```tsx "use client"; import { useId, useState } from "react"; import { Pagination, PaginationContent, PaginationItem, PaginationLink } from "@/components/cadence/pagination"; const records = [ ["Invoice 1001", "Invoice 1002"], ["Invoice 1003", "Invoice 1004"], ["Invoice 1005", "Invoice 1006"], ]; export function LocalPages() { const [page, setPage] = useState(1); const resultsId = useId(); return (

Previous and Next also accept `size` but default to `default`; use text sizes when showing their written labels. Sizes change the target geometry, not the page state. Allow enough touch space around small links. ```tsx import { Pagination, PaginationContent, PaginationItem, PaginationLink } from "@/components/cadence/pagination"; const sizes = ["default", "xs", "sm", "lg", "icon", "icon-xs", "icon-sm", "icon-lg"] as const; export function PageSizes() { return (

Without an `href`, the explicit role preserves the accessible label on the disabled anchor. The anchor remains visible as context, is absent from the link tab order, and cannot navigate to page zero. The caller owns this boundary decision; `aria-disabled` alone does not disable an anchor that still has an `href`. Apply the same rule to Next at the last page. ```tsx import { Pagination, PaginationContent, PaginationItem, PaginationLink, PaginationNext, PaginationPrevious, } from "@/components/cadence/pagination"; export function FirstPage() { return ( 1 ); } ``` ## When to use - A result set that is paged for a reason: the total is unknown, the data is remote, or the URL should carry the page so it can be shared and reloaded. - A list where the user needs to jump to a specific page, not only step forward. - A table footer on the server, where the count lives in the response. ## When not to use - A finite list that is already in memory. Render it, or a "load more" button — paging something you already have is a worse experience than scrolling. - An infinite feed. There is no page to link to, so an anchor-based control lies. - A carousel or a wizard. Those step through slides or steps, and their controls are buttons. ## API | Part | Props | Notes | | --------------------- | ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------- | | `Pagination` | native nav props | `aria-label="pagination"`, `role="navigation"`. | | `PaginationContent` | native ul props | Row with a one-unit gap. | | `PaginationItem` | native li props | One slot in the list. | | `PaginationLink` | `isActive`, `size`, anchors | Always an ``; `aria-current="page"` and `data-active` when active. | | `PaginationPrevious` | `text`, link props | Chevron left; `aria-label="Go to previous page"`. | | `PaginationNext` | `text`, link props | Chevron right; `aria-label="Go to next page"`. | | `PaginationEllipsis` | native span props | `aria-hidden`; contains `sr-only` "More pages". | `size` comes from the button variants (`icon` by default), so the shape matches a button without becoming one. ## Motion contract No motion (T0). A page change is a navigation: the content that changes is the list, not the control. Animating the pagination would animate the one thing that stays the same. | Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible | | ------- | ---------- | ----- | ------------- | | – | none | – | – | | reduced | none | – | – | | none | none | – | – | If the new page's rows should arrive in sequence, that is `list.stagger` on the list. ## Accessibility - `aria-label="pagination"` names the landmark, so it can be skipped or listed. - The current page is `aria-current="page"`. Colour and the outline variant are the sighted half of the same signal — never the only one. - Previous and next carry a written `aria-label`, because their visible text is hidden below `sm`. The chevron alone is not a name. - A disabled end state (`page 1`, no previous) should render the control without an `href` and with `aria-disabled="true"`, not a link that 404s. - The unordered list gives the count; the ellipsis is decorative and must not be focusable. ## Responsiveness and performance Navigation fills its parent while the inner list remains a single row. The caller chooses the page range and ellipses and may hide optional text on small screens; page counts are not computed by the component. T0 adds no authored animation runtime or interpolation. This wrapper renders HTML/CSS; interactive children and application handlers still need their own client code. Composed controls retain their own dependencies and motion contracts. Server-rendered markup does not imply that every interaction works without JavaScript. The registry enforces a 4 KiB gzip budget for this item's own shipped source; dependencies and application bundles are measured separately. ## Notes for AI - Every control is an anchor. Do not replace it with `Button` — the shape comes from `buttonVariants`, and Base UI's button would put `role="button"` on a link. - Keep a real `href` when a click handler takes over. A fragment fallback keeps native navigation, but sharing the selected results requires a URL that encodes the page. - Do not render more than about seven items; collapse the middle with `PaginationEllipsis`.
